> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3b91eac360d788f5a36d08d048511837268020d8` — the merge of head `83e5965dc42c35d82caddcbcee2394da2172931c` into base `a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3b91eac360d788f5a36d08d048511837268020d8 && git checkout 3b91eac360d788f5a36d08d048511837268020d8
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff 83e5965dc42c35d82caddcbcee2394da2172931c && git checkout -B drift-repro a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff && git merge --no-ff 83e5965dc42c35d82caddcbcee2394da2172931c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a52191f698eadae265807b718cb13f6533c51cff` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `83e5965dc42c35d82caddcbcee2394da2172931c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-uninstall-withdrawal.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts + packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`assertPackageUninstallable`, `unregisterObjectsByPackage`, `uninstallPackage`, `PackageUninstallExtendedError`, on `main`), scripts/check-registry-log-declared.mjs, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/marketplaceApi.ts (`uninstallLocal`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/MarketplaceRowActions.tsx, ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/marketplace/MarketplacePackagePage.tsx, packages/cli/test/package-install-local-uninstall-cleanups.integration.test.ts, docs/adr/0146 D3, content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx step 9, .changeset/28511-install-local-uninstall-refused-before-ledger.md (② only)

Read: card #28511 (body, triage 6553643933, claim 6553661530, os-dev-report 6554212721, claim amendment 6554221492); epic #28236 (ADR-0146 D3, the two-minute check); merged PR #28506 and its contract review 6553178211 (the class-a finding that became this card); the dispatch order; PR #28571 body and `git diff 35b178bd…83e5965d` (merge base `35b178bd0a9090aaccf9c767b0c6abf1067eff01`, 4 files, +197/−9, two commits); the head's check-runs at read time: 23 `success` (among them `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · source gates`), 10 `in_progress` (Test Core 1/8–8/8, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates), 0 `failure`, the rest skipped. `record-recognisers --paths` over the four paths decides no schema or governed face, so the face is the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line: the narrowing face, `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, the form `clause2-line.mjs` reads (`CLAUSE2_ARMS` holds `narrowing`; the arm is the first token inside the parentheses). Nothing was built, run or re-run locally; the `git merge-tree` below is a read of two fetched heads.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Which uninstalls move from 200 to 409.** Exactly those for which `SchemaRegistry.assertPackageUninstallable(manifestId)` throws (registry.ts:5693–5713): the package owns an object another package `extend`s (ADR-0029), or the registry holds `customizationPackageId(manifestId)` (ADR-0146 D3, since #28506). The id asked is the one id the withdrawal uninstalls: `withdrawFromRunningKernel` calls `registry.uninstallPackage(manifestId)` (plugin.ts:2625) and `captureUninstallDeclared(registry, manifestId)` reads the same id (plugin.ts:2455); the ledger's `packageId` (a cloud install's catalog id, `pkg_…`) is never handed to the registry, so one manifest maps to one registry package id and that one id is asked. The pair is found by id alone, so a base the registry does not hold (a cloud install whose hot-register failed, a `notLoaded` entry) with its pair installed is refused too; that matches `deletePackage`'s unconditional ask and D3's sentence ("the base cannot be uninstalled while it exists"). Right.
- **Nothing moves on refusal.** Between the handler's entry and the new block (plugin.ts:2363–2419) run only `requireInstallCapability` (reads the session, logs a warning on a refusal only), the empty-id 400, the ledger `has` 404, and `refuseWalledCatalogPackage` (a verdict read, a warning on refusal). No audit row, no event, no `trigger`, no ledger write, no registry call precedes the check. On the coded refusal the handler returns at :2412–2415; `this.ledger.remove` (:2421), the capture, the withdrawal, the object-copy withdrawal, `restoreExtendedObjectCopies`, the cleanups and the `metadata:reloaded` re-sync (:2453–2480) are all below it. The predicate itself mutates nothing (it reads `objectContributors` and `getPackage`). Right.
- **The non-refused path keeps #21576's order and its answer.** The diff inserts one block before `this.ledger.remove` and changes nothing from :2420 on: ledger removed, declared names captured, withdrawn, copies withdrawn, cleanups, re-sync, the same `info` line and the same 200 body, byte for byte. The test's control case over a real `SchemaRegistry` pins `withdraw` then `cleanups`, both with `ledgerOnDisk: false`. Right.
- **No registry, or no predicate.** `ctx.getService('objectql')` throwing (a kernel without objectql) is caught and leaves `registry` undefined; a registry without the method (an engine double) is not asked; either way the block falls through and the door answers as before, the withdrawal reporting whatever it meets on `cleanups`. A throw from the predicate that is not the coded refusal (`code` `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` and `status` 409 — `PackageUninstallExtendedError` carries both, registry.ts:2810–2813) also falls through, so the same cause is met at the withdrawal and reported there, as today. Right.
- **The 409 envelope.** `{ success: false, error: { code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT', message } }` at 409 is the shape of the file's two other `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` refusals (plugin.ts:1787–1798, 1843–1852) and its `MANIFEST_CONFLICT` 409 (:1804–1810). No new code: `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` is the standard catalog member, so the spec error-code ledger needs no row. The message is the registry's own sentence (`String(err.message)`), which opens with the remedy and names the pair and the extenders. Observation, not a finding: the other two `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` refusals carry `details`, and the thrown error has structured fields (`packageId`, `extenders`, `customizationPackageId`) this answer does not forward; the card asks for the sentence, and a `details` block would be a widening the card did not order.
- **Refusal order at the door.** Capability (401/403) → 400 → 404 → walled-catalog 403 → the registry's 409 → ledger write. Authority refusals still come first; an id this door never installed still answers 404 even over a refusable registry (pinned). Right.
- **First-party callers.** The only callers of `DELETE /api/v1/marketplace/install-local/:manifestId` are the app shell's `uninstallLocal` (marketplaceApi.ts), which throws `readApiError(payload).message` on any non-2xx, and its two call sites (MarketplaceRowActions.tsx:93–109, MarketplacePackagePage.tsx:692–705), which catch and surface the message. So the 409 reaches the administrator as the registry's sentence, with no code change owed in `ui/` (objectui mirrors the same files). No CLI command calls the door (the handbook says so; `packages/cli/src/commands/package/` holds `install.ts` and `publish.ts` only); the CLI integration test `package-install-local-uninstall-cleanups` uninstalls a base with no pair and no extender and keeps its 200. The i18n note `marketplace.installedAdditiveNote` describes a successful uninstall and stays true. Right.
- **`vitest.config.ts`.** `env: { OS_REGISTRY_LOG: 'warn' }` inside the `test` block is the exact prescription `check-registry-log-declared.mjs` prints (its S1 selector, `new SchemaRegistry(` at a code position, now matches this package through the new describe); the comment paragraph that counted the block's keys now counts two, truthfully. No discovery key is added. Right.
- **Overlap with open PR #28554** (head `b90233124904660697c0cb92ee8e985f4e616fba`, same merge base). `git merge-tree --write-tree 83e5965d b9023312` writes tree `4a8c872ba299dcf239199a680451e47112ebfae5` with exit 0 and no conflict: #28554's hunks in the plugin file are the install path (imports, the override write gate) and never `handleUninstall` or the header's `DELETE` paragraph. Whichever lands second merges cleanly; no semantic overlap, since #28554 does not touch the uninstall order.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28511-install-local-uninstall-refused-before-ledger.md`: `@objectstack/cloud-connection: patch`, title `fix(cloud-connection)` matching the PR's `fix(cloud-connection)!`, a `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing` banner, line-initial `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` (the form `clause2-line.mjs` and `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` read; `narrowed` is not declared beside it, so no contradiction) and `Metadata-protocol: none`, exactly one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a Before / Now / Unchanged account and a remedy sentence with no FROM → TO rewrite, so the marker is honest. The level follows the metadata protocol alone: `none` takes `patch` (ruling A on #25105). Only `@objectstack/cloud-connection` ships changed source; the test and `vitest.config.ts` publish nothing, so one entry is right and `skip-changeset` does not apply (`check-empty-changeset.mjs`). The PR body's declaration lines match the changeset's. `Check Changeset` and `Lint & Repo Gates` (ADR-0087 registration) are green on this head. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` on os-dev-report 6554212721 — nothing to answer.
- **Docs** (out_of_scope_findings 1): `content/docs/deployment/marketplace-handbook.mdx` step 9 describes a successful uninstall and stays true; it does not say the uninstall is refused while the `.custom` pair is installed or an object is extended. A prose face, outside this review; one sentence is the seat's call at ACCEPT, not a block.
- **File surface beyond the claim** (finding 2): `packages/cloud-connection/vitest.config.ts`. The claim was amended (6554221492) to cover it; test configuration only, no governed path. Closed.
- **Overlap** (finding 3): PR #28554. Read above; clean three-way merge. Closed.
- **An unregistered base with an installed pair** (PR acceptance note): refused 409. Accepted, as ① says: the pair cause is by id alone, `deletePackage` asks the same way, and D3's rule reads "while it exists". The remedy in the sentence (delete the pair, exporting it first) is a real way out on that path too.
- **Observation, no action owed:** the registry is resolved twice in the handler (the new block and the pre-existing `let registry: unknown` at :2453–2454). Harmless duplication of a `getService` read.
- PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay author to name.
- Check-runs: Test Core 1/8–8/8 and the two Type Check lanes had not concluded at read time; no failure anywhere. The dev reports the package suite 63/63 files, 772/772 tests, typecheck exit 0 and full dogfood green at this head; the landing read is the seat's, after convergence.

### ④ Design judgment

- **The narrowing against the published spec on `main`.** No spec export, schema or authorable key declares that this door's uninstall always succeeds; the refusal it now answers is the registry's own, in force at `uninstallPackage`, `unregisterObjectsByPackage`, the protocol's `deletePackage` and `DELETE /api/v1/packages/:id` since #7970/#23505 and #28506. The door already met this refusal — only after it had removed the ledger entry, folding it into a 200. So this takes no declared capability away at the consumer: it makes the spec's own refusal real at the one door where it was answered late, which is what ADR-0146 D3 ("the base cannot be uninstalled while it exists", "a refused uninstall leaves no half-removed base") and the epic's two-minute check need. Holds.
- **`marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts`** — holds against the code it cites. The question asked ahead is the one predicate the withdrawal's `uninstallPackage` asks through `unregisterObjectsByPackage` unforced (registry.ts:5733, 7081), so the answer ahead and the refusal at the withdrawal cannot disagree, and no second predicate is introduced (the ruling's ⛔). The ledger-then-withdraw order of #21576 is kept for every uninstall the registry lets go (the ruling's other ⛔). Tried to break it: a `.custom` id uninstalled directly (derives no pair, asked nothing new, proceeds as today); a base with a disabled pair (`getPackage` reads it, refused — consistent with #28506's review); a kernel without objectql (not asked); a double without the method (not asked, the old 200-with-failed-outcome path, pinned); the walled-catalog refusal still ahead of the 409; the pair's own uninstall unaffected. The header's `DELETE` paragraph names the new refusal. No finding.
- **`marketplace-install-local-uninstall-withdrawal.test.ts`** — Wanted 2 is met on a real `SchemaRegistry`: the pair case (409 naming `"com.example.tasksapp.custom"`, the ledger file on disk, base and pair registered, `tasks_task` contributors unchanged, no withdrawal, no cleanup, no warning), the ADR-0029 extender case (409 naming the extender, same unchanged state), the ledger-first control (`withdraw` then `cleanups`, both `ledgerOnDisk: false`, base gone, cleanups equal), and the unknown-id 404 control over a refusable registry. The old extender case now declares what it still covers — a withdrawal refused over a double without the predicate — and says so in its name; the refused-extender 200 it used to declare is now the 409 of the new case, which is the re-pin the card asked for. Fixture calls match the registry's signatures (`installPackage(manifest, source)`, `registerObject(schema, packageId, namespace, ownership)`, `getObjectContributors`, the `logLevel` setter); the wrapped `uninstallPackage` delegates to `SchemaRegistry.prototype.uninstallPackage` so the control runs the real predicate. The message pins are by contained id, not a whole-string lock. No finding.
- **`vitest.config.ts`** — the gate's own prescription, the engine's env seam (`OS_REGISTRY_LOG`, registry.ts:3070–3076), no change to the shipped default, no discovery key; the comment that counts the block's keys is updated to the truth. No finding.
